name: mqtt
description: A native MQTT 3.1.1 and 5.0 client and the kernel's PubSubPort over it. The packet codec, the topic validator and the client state machine are testable without a broker; the transport is one class built on PHP streams so OpenSwoole's coroutine hooks apply. MQTT is length-prefixed and binary, so a topic cannot append a command the way a NATS subject can — the hazards are elsewhere: a Variable Byte Integer that claims 268 MB, a wildcard in a PUBLISH topic that silently reaches nobody, and a Client Identifier reused across processes, which the broker resolves by disconnecting the process that had it.
//daemon: DELIBERATELY ABSENT. `daemon` pins a SHA-256 per platform and refuses a platform it has no digest for, which needs a broker that publishes one verifiable archive per platform — and no MQTT broker does: mosquitto cuts no GitHub releases at all, NanoMQ ships linux .deb/.rpm only, EMQX has no macOS tarball, mochi-mqtt ships no binaries. Inventing an unverified download path for this one plugin would put a hole in the mechanism every other plugin relies on. README 'Getting a broker' lists the three real options, one of which is the nats-server this toolchain ALREADY pins — it speaks MQTT 3.1.1 natively, so a project running the NATS plugin adds a listener rather than a second daemon.

config.//will: A will is the broker publishing on this client's behalf when it disappears without a clean DISCONNECT, which is how a status topic stays correct without anybody polling. MQTT_WILL_TOPIC alone turns it on; the other four are meaningless without it, so they are commented out by default rather than given values.
